output.brief: Pellacott's 2026 VA-220 valves are the problem, not the installers or the firmware. Brenmoor's lab matched claims to each unit's valve, installer and firmware. Pellacott valves fail at about 41–42 claims per 1,000 whichever installer fitted them and whichever firmware ran. Durrant-Hale valves stay at 5–7 in every group. Unused warehouse Pellacott 2026 valves leak at the seat in 11% of cases, against 1% for 2025 builds. The independent calibration visit found Pellacott's leak-test rig out of service since January 2026 and no VA-220 test program on any other rig. The 2026 certificates repeat four sets of values, and the same sets appear in November 2025 certificates. So the certificates that lifted the score to 89 do not reflect real tests. Do not release the six held lots on fresh certificates, and do not penalise the installers. Quarantine 2026 Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and test valves with Brenmoor's own helium test before release. Make Pellacott's claims of testing verifiable. Check other suppliers' records, because their conformance scores also rose. The seal change and the new assembly line cannot yet be separated, so hold off on telling Pellacott to go back to the old seal supplier until that is resolved. I'm fairly confident in this.
